key_insight: An incremental Deep Energy Method can model ductile fracture by coupling J2 plasticity and phase-field damage with separate neural representations for displacement and crack phase-field.
engineering_relevance: This provides a mesh-light alternative for predicting fracture initiation and growth in elasto-plastic solids while retaining key constitutive history effects.
method: Alternates energy minimization for displacement and phase-field variables at each load increment.
Uses a ReZero residual network for displacement and localized Gaussian radial basis functions for the phase field.
Updates plastic history locally with radial return and carries constitutive state forward via transfer learning.
evidence_signal: The method matches finite-element reference results closely for force-displacement response, energy evolution, plastic deformation, and crack propagation.
watch_item: Accuracy becomes more sensitive to the size of loading increments near abrupt fracture events, so stable increment control is important.
paper_title: A deep energy method formulation for phase-field modelling of ductile fracture
